ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Jeffrey shoots three arrows at each of four identical targets. He scores 29 points on the first target, 43 on the second and 47 on the third. How many points does Jeffrey score on the last target?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Jeffrey shoots three arrows at each of four identical targets. He scores 29 points on the first target, 43 on the second and 47 on the third. How many points does Jeffrey score on the last target?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the picture there are four identical three-ring targets, and each target has 3 arrows on it. Looking according to the positions where the arrows land on the outer ring, middle ring, and inner ring: the 1st target has 1 arrow in the outer ring and 2 arrows in the middle ring; the 2nd target has 1 arrow in the outer ring and 2 arrows in the inner ring; the 3rd target has 1 arrow in the middle ring and 2 arrows in the inner ring; the 4th target has 1 arrow in the outer ring, 1 arrow in the middle ring, and 1 arrow in the inner ring. Then reason: Let the scores of the outer ring, middle ring, and inner ring be o, m, and i respectively. From the scores of the first three targets, we can get: o + 2m = 29, o + 2i = 43, m + 2i = 47. From o = 29 - 2m, substituting into o + 2i = 43 gives 29 - 2m + 2i = 43, that is, i - m = 7, so i = m + 7. Substituting into m + 2i = 47, we get m + 2(m + 7) = 47, that is, 3m + 14 = 47, so m = 11. Thus i = 18, o = 29 - 2×11 = 7. The score of the last target is o + m + i = 7 + 11 + 18 = 36.
